spokenLines.description: Exact spoken-word ledger copied from the owning scene plan. Keep one bare, verbatim string per line; use an empty array when nobody speaks. Do not add <d> markup or language labels here.

style.description: One or two sentences of VISUAL STYLE only — medium, palette, light quality, finish — taken from the supplied art style. The runner emits it immediately before [Shot 1], which is where the official full-reference guide puts the style opening. No action, no character, no camera here.

summary.description: The summary section. Start with a task-type prefix such as [reference generation], then summarize the target video and shot flow using only the Subject labels the runner will inject.

references.description: Ordered visible references for this scene. Put the most important subjects first and the location last. Every entry must be used by at least one shot.

id.description: The exact story-bible id. Use the plain character/object/location id, never a generated state id.

appearsAs.description: Short visual description of the current visible reference, as a lower-case noun phrase. The runner drops it into '<Subject N> is ___ in <Picture N>.'

job.description: What this plate must HOLD VISUALLY, as a lower-case noun phrase — the concrete features to preserve ('her face, the lava forearm texture and the copper-wire hair'). NOT a narrative role: 'the defiant smith refusing to surrender the Ember' tells the renderer nothing to preserve. The runner drops it into 'Follow it for ___.'

shots.description: Ordered time-bounded beats. startTime values are cut times in seconds: the first is 0 and every later value is strictly greater than the previous one. endTime must be greater than startTime and no greater than duration. The runner enforces these relationships.

composition.description: Framing, viewpoint, scale and where each visible subject is — ONE definite answer. Never offer alternatives ('in the background or periphery'): the renderer cannot choose, so an either/or becomes a smear.

acting.description: REQUIRED on every shot. This is the list of CHARACTERS in the shot: one entry per character, and a character is in the shot if and only if they have an entry here. Only character reference ids, never an object or location. Use [] for a shot with no character in it.

subjectId.description: Character reference id adapted in this shot.

tactic.description: Concrete action verb describing how the character pursues the objective now.

observableBehavior.description: Filmable behavior in the body, gaze, breath, hands, voice or reaction; never an emotion label alone.

beatChange.description: Visible behavior change that marks the new beat.

reaction.description: Optional listening or partner reaction that begins before or during the partner's line.

assessmentMoment.description: Optional visible moment in which the character takes in important information before choosing the next action.

interruptedAction.description: Optional physical business that stops or changes as the beat lands.

sceneryIds.description: The OBJECT and LOCATION references visible in this shot. Never a character — characters enter a shot only through acting[]. Use [] when the shot shows no object or location.

action.description: The physical state change: what is true at the start and what is true at the end.

cameraAmplitude.description: Optional second camera dimension (base guide 4.3). Omit for medium amplitude.

cameraSpeed.description: Optional third camera dimension (base guide 4.3). Omit for normal speed.

sound.description: Physical, shot-synchronous sound only. Keep scene-wide ambience in overallSoundscape.

transition.description: For later shots, the cut written as a lower-case clause that continues "At 00:04.000, …", ideally opening with a documented cut phrase (the shot cuts to / the camera cuts to / the shot transitions to). Say what NEW information the cut reveals. The runner repairs capitalisation and supplies the cut verb if missing.

dialogue.description: Typed lines owned by this shot. Each exactWords value must match exactly one entry in spokenLines; the runner emits the H3 <d> tag without changing it.

speakerId.description: Stable voice id such as S1. The same speaker keeps the same id throughout the scene.

subjectId.description: The visible reference id that owns this voice.

exactWords.description: Copy the corresponding spokenLines string verbatim, including punctuation and native script.

delivery.description: Vocal delivery placed outside the dialogue tag, such as quietly or with a strained breath.

voicePrompt.description: The speaker's fixed vocal identity, copied VERBATIM from that character's character_acting_profile. Required on every line; the runner emits it once, before the subject's first line.

offScreen.description: True when the speaker is heard but not seen in this shot. REQUIRED to be true for any speaker who has no acting entry in this shot, since acting[] is what puts a character on screen. The runner then writes the official off-screen voiceover phrasing.

overallSoundscape.description: One short paragraph of scene-wide non-verbal ambience, physical action sounds and breathing. Never repeat dialogue, singing or score. Use N/A only for genuine silence.

nonDiegeticMusic.description: Score the characters cannot hear: instrumentation, pace, rhythm and dynamic change. Use N/A when there is no score.

negatives.description: Explicit negative directions that the runner will write into the positive H3 prose because this graph has no negative-conditioning input.

duration.description: Total seconds for this one H3 call. Every shot must fit inside it.

speechSeconds.description: Your estimate of how many seconds the SPOKEN audio takes end to end: every word at the pace the voice profile and delivery imply, plus the pauses you intend between sentences. Exclude lead-in and tail — the renderer adds those. It raises the clip length when it is longer than the renderer's own estimate, and can never shorten it, so a generous number costs a little dead air while a mean one cuts the last words off. Read the voicePrompt: 'slow pace, gravelly, deliberate pauses' is far slower than the ~2.8 words/second a plain reading assumes. Use 0 when nobody speaks.

purpose.description: The single story beat this scene lands.

shotStructure.description: Use multi_cut for two or more shots; use continuous_moving or locked_single for exactly one shot. The runner enforces the count and timing rules.

renderComplexity.description: How hard this scene is to RENDER — not how important it is to the story. This sets the sampler step count, so it costs real time: simple=4 steps, moderate=6, complex=8, extreme=10. Judge it on what the renderer has to resolve: how many bodies are moving at once, how fast they move, how much fire/smoke/debris/particle work there is, how much fine texture has to survive being in motion, and how many surfaces interact with a moving light source. simple = one or two figures, contained movement, stable light (a held beat, a conversation, a hand on an object). moderate = several figures or one demanding element (a fast camera move, one effect, a crowd held in the background). complex = many moving figures AND an effect, or combat, or fire lighting the surfaces around it. extreme = a mass of figures in motion with heavy effects and dynamic light — a melee, a collapse, a firestorm. A quiet scene marked extreme wastes GPU; a battle marked simple renders as mush. Do not inflate it for dramatic weight.

objective.description: What the character wants in this scene, expressed as a verb aimed at a specific partner or concrete target.

stakes.description: The concrete cost of failing in this scene.

physicalBusiness.description: The physical task or object-work that gives the performance a life beyond the words.

bodyState.description: Observable center of gravity, posture, tempo, openness and breath at scene start.

eyeLife.description: Observable target changes, micro-saccades, blink quality, catchlights and eyes-leading-thought behavior.

subtext.description: Optional behaviorally legible difference between what is said and what is pursued.

statusDynamic.description: Optional visible change in who takes or yields status.

proxemics.description: Optional motivated distance relationship and changes between the characters.

continuationAnchor.description: The state this scene ENDS in, written so the NEXT scene can open on it. Required. This is the forward half of the continuity chain — it is not rendered into this scene.

fixedLandmarks.description: Fixed set features and where they sit ON SCREEN. 'the stove is in the kitchen' is useless; 'the stove is in the left third against the back wall' is the entry, because only that survives being handed to the next scene.

name.description: The landmark, named as it appears: 'the gas stove', 'the wooden table', 'the doorway to the hallway'.

screenPosition.description: Where it sits in frame: 'in the left third against the back wall', 'across the centre-bottom foreground'.

characterPositions.description: Everyone VISIBLE at this boundary. Must use reference ids declared in references[].

screenPosition.description: Where in frame: 'in the left third, midground'.

facing.description: Which way they face: 'three-quarters away from camera'.

pose.description: What their body is doing: 'standing at the stove, palm flat on the counter'.

offStage.description: Everyone NOT in frame at this boundary, so the next scene knows they must be seen to ARRIVE rather than appearing already present. State position and reason ONLY — never speech. 'she calls from the hallway' with no dialogue line synthesises voice with no words and is rejected.

where.description: Where they physically are: 'in the unlit hallway beyond the doorway'.

reason.description: Why they are off screen: 'she has not come in yet'. No speech verbs.

lightingBaseline.description: The light in force at this boundary — key/fill/rim direction and quality, plus any modifier: 'a hard cool tubelight from directly overhead, with a warm stove flame on the left'. The next scene inherits this unless it declares a change.

propStates.description: HANDLED props and their state at this boundary — poured, moved, held, set down. This is the field the shipped soap contradicted itself on: scene 1 ended with the tea poured and steaming and scene 2 opened asserting the cups were not yet visible.

state.description: Its state: 'both poured and steaming, on the table'.

continuationFrom.description: The state this scene OPENS on, copied from the PREVIOUS scene's continuationAnchor (supplied to you as context). Omit ONLY on the first scene of the film. This is what stops a character appearing without arriving and the set moving between cuts.

hardCut.description: Set ONLY when this scene deliberately breaks from the previous one — a time skip, a new location, a reset: 'two hours later, the same kitchen'. Discontinuity is legitimate; UNDECLARED discontinuity is the defect. When set, describe the new opening state in the fields below rather than the inherited one.

description: Strict structured intermediate scene contract for MiniMax H3. The runner deterministically writes subject_definitions and retention_analysis from references, compiles shots and typed dialogue into detailed_description, and assembles the existing six official sections. Do not author subject-definition prose or any <Picture N> slot numbering; those are runner-owned.
